cards.explanation: The answer is: The Nile is mine and I made it myself. That's the brag, word for word: "The Nile is mine; I made it myself." (Ezekiel 29:3) Pharaoh, Egypt's king, takes all the credit. That's like a guy walking into my bakery and announcing he invented the oven. Friends, sit DOWN.

The answer is: the fish of his streams. God says it plainly: "I will haul you up out of your rivers, and all the fish of your streams will cling to your scales." (Ezekiel 29:4) So the fish come along for the ride. Nobody asked those fish if they wanted to go. I think they had a rough trip.

The answer is False. God says, "You will fall on the open field and will not be taken away or gathered for burial." (Ezekiel 29:5) Nobody comes to pick him up. That's a heavy line, so I'll just let it sit.

The answer is: that He is the LORD. That's the whole point. God says, "Then all the people of Egypt will know that I am the LORD." (Ezekiel 29:6) Pharaoh said the Nile was his own work. By the end, everybody in Egypt knows who the LORD is.

The answer is reeds: "…you were only a staff of reeds to the house of Israel." (Ezekiel 29:6) A reed looks like a walking stick until you put your weight on it. Then it's a bad day for your shoulders.

The answer is: it splinters and tears their shoulders. God says, "When Israel took hold of you with their hands, you splintered, tearing all their shoulders…" (Ezekiel 29:7) They grabbed it for help and it hurt them instead. That's a rough trade, friends.

The answer is True. God says, "I will bring a sword against you and cut off from you man and beast." (Ezekiel 29:8) This is a hard word. It's the Lord GOD speaking about Egypt, and He says it plainly.

The answer is rivers. After the Nile brag, God says, "…therefore I am against you and against your rivers." (Ezekiel 29:10) Pharaoh claimed the river as his own work. So the rivers get named right alongside him.

The answer is: no man or beast will pass through. God says, "No foot of man or beast will pass through, and it will be uninhabited for forty years." (Ezekiel 29:11) Not one foot, friends. It's about as quiet as a bakery after the last cookie is gone.

The answer is False. The land is uninhabited for forty years, and God says, "…I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries." (Ezekiel 29:12) They're spread out, not together at home.

The answer is: He gathers them back from the nations. God says, "At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the nations to which they were scattered." (Ezekiel 29:13) After all that scattering, there's a gathering. I like how the story doesn't stop at the hard part.

The answer is lowly: "There they will be a lowly kingdom." (Ezekiel 29:14) They're back in Pathros, the land of their origin, but not on top. God goes further in the next verse, calling Egypt "…the lowliest of kingdoms…" (Ezekiel 29:15)

The answer is False. God says Egypt "…will never again exalt itself above the nations." and adds, "…I will diminish Egypt so that it will never again rule over the nations." (Ezekiel 29:15) Egypt does get to come home to Pathros, where "…they will be a lowly kingdom." (Ezekiel 29:14) It gets to come home, but not to the top.

The answer is: their sin in turning to Egypt. God says Egypt "…will remind them of their iniquity in turning to the Egyptians." (Ezekiel 29:16) Iniquity is sin. So Egypt stops being a place to lean and becomes a reminder of leaning in the wrong place.

The answer is False. The text says Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and his army "…received no wages from Tyre for the labor they expended on it." (Ezekiel 29:18) Tyre is the city they worked against. That's a lot of hard work with nothing in the envelope.

The answers are Egypt and wages. God says, "I will give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon…" (Ezekiel 29:19) Pharaoh was king of Egypt, so that's where this land change is headed. And God says, "This will be the wages for his army." (Ezekiel 29:19) The army worked and didn't get paid by Tyre, and here God names where the pay comes from.

The answer is: because the labor was done for God. God says, "I have given him the land of Egypt as the reward for his labor, because it was done for Me…" (Ezekiel 29:20) That's the reason, and it's stated right there. The labor was for Him.
The answer is True. God says, "…I will open your mouth to speak among them." (Ezekiel 29:21) He's talking to Ezekiel here. I think that's a nice way to end a heavy chapter.
